test_focus: does the CONTENT of injected dreams matter — engineering-craft seeds (new, Phase 15) vs computing-history seeds (existing) on technical-debugging prompts. The Phase 14 finding established imagination injection hurts on technical (28% win vs control); Phase 15 asks whether domain-appropriate content can claw that back.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

examples: The 3am page where the on-call engineer found the bug had been live for six years.
The git bisect that ended at the merge commit whose author had left the company.
The retry policy that worked perfectly for three years, until the downstream API added a 429 response code.
The feature flag that was meant to be temporary in 2017 and is now load-bearing.
implementation_added.domain_preference_change: engineering domain now prefers engineering-craft FIRST, computing-history second. Research domain gets engineering-craft as secondary.

arms: engineering-craft (EC): 5-dream archive seeded with 'the bug live for six years' and similar texture
computing-history (CH): 5-dream archive seeded with Hamilton, Knuth, Engelbart, Hopper, Thompson + Ritchie imagery
experiment_design.judge_design: Direct EC-vs-CH head-to-head. Both arms use the neutral wrapper (engineering routing). Response order randomized per trial.
experiment_design.no_control_baseline: Phase 14 already gave us tight CI on no-injection control vs treatment; Phase 15 is specifically asking which seeds win.

results.interpretation: Engineering-craft win rate 62.9% with 95% CI [51%, 73%]. The lower bound JUST exceeds 50%, so the EC > CH effect is statistically significant at alpha=0.05 (one-sided). The directional finding is clear: domain-appropriate dream content lifts the imagination-injection effect on engineering prompts.

implications: **The CONTENT of the dream archive matters — not just the wrapper.** When an engineering agent dreams of 'the bug that had been live for six years' instead of 'Margaret Hamilton at the Apollo console,' the resulting injections score better on engineering-prompt judgments.

**The wins concentrate on scenarios where the engineering-craft texture maps directly to the prompt.** retry-under-load (90% EC win — the new 'retry policy that worked for three years until...' seed maps cleanly), legacy-deletion (90% — the 'feature flag from 2017 is now load-bearing' seed maps), refactor-decision (70% — the 'TODO from 2014 wrong in opposite direction' seed maps).

**The one CH win (python-memory-creep at 30% EC) suggests historical-figure framing can still help on some prompts.** Computing-history seeds aren't useless; they're just not the strongest default for engineering work.

**Phase 14 + 15 together strongly justify the routing layer.** Phase 14: domain-aware *wrapper* selection avoids the technical-prompt penalty. Phase 15: domain-aware *content* selection further lifts the technical-prompt win rate above what neutral-wrapper-with-historical-seeds achieves.

**The shipped engineering preference order (engineering-craft FIRST, computing-history second) is justified by data.** The CI lower bound is just above 50%, so this is statistically significant — but the per-scenario heterogeneity (30% to 90%) shows the effect varies a lot by prompt shape.

**This is a domain-content story, not a generic 'better seeds' story.** Engineering-craft seeds are specifically tuned to engineering work; they would likely lose on creative prompts the same way computing-history wins do.

**Combined with Phase 14: imagination injection on engineering prompts now has a path forward.** With engineering-craft seeds + neutral wrapper, we'd estimate a treatment-win rate somewhere between Phase 14's 28% and the EC/CH ratio implies — possibly 35-45% — still below 50% vs no-injection but materially better than the historical-figure default.

feature_verdicts.engineering_craft_seed_library: sings — 62.9% win rate vs computing-history on engineering prompts, lower CI bound above 50%
feature_verdicts.domain_aware_seed_selection: sings — engineering-craft as primary engineering preference justified by data
feature_verdicts.imagination_injection_on_engineering_pro: improved — likely closes part of Phase 14's 28% gap (combined experiment in future phase)

known_limitations: Phase 15 did not include a no-injection control arm — we don't know whether eng-craft injection beats no-injection control. The implicit claim ('eng-craft lifts the Phase-14 28% rate') is inferred from the EC > CH delta, not directly measured. A future combined experiment would test eng-craft vs no-injection control directly.
N=10 per scenario is still modest. Some per-scenario CIs are wide (e.g. permission-denied-chmod: [31%, 83%]).
verdict: WIN — domain-appropriate dream CONTENT helps. Engineering agents should dream of engineering-craft, not historical-figures-in-computing.
next_steps: Phase 16 (suggested): combined experiment — control vs treatment-with-engineering-craft on technical prompts (N=20). Does engineering-craft + neutral wrapper close enough of Phase 14's 28% gap to make imagination injection net-positive for engineering agents?

Phase 17 (suggested): per-call routing. The 90% EC-win on retry-under-load and legacy-deletion vs 30% on memory-creep shows even within 'technical' there's prompt-shape variance. A per-prompt classifier could route the right seeds to each prompt.
Phase 18 (suggested): write more engineering-craft seeds (toward 30+ entries). The library at 15 entries will repeat fairly quickly under a daily-dreaming engineer.
